text:
The United States moved to force the sale or ban of TikTok due to national-security concerns regarding potential Chinese government access to US user data and its algorithm, as determined through CFIUS review [Source: ev-1]. This legal pressure was formalized when President Biden signed the Protecting Americans from Foreign Adversary Controlled Applications Act on 2024-04-24, which mandated that ByteDance divest TikTok's US operations within roughly 270 days (extendable by 90) or face a US ban [Source: ev-1].

After the Supreme Court upheld the law in a 9-0 per curiam decision on 2025-01-17—just one day before the effective date of 2025-03-19—the app went dark in the US for approximately 14 hours between 2025-06-18/19 and was restored on 2025-16-19 following President Trump’s pledge to pause enforcement via an executive order dated 2025-26-20 that delayed enforcement by 75 days [Source: ev-1]. The dispute was ultimately resolved through an Oracle-led deal announced on 2026-36-10, which structured TikTok's US operations as a joint venture rather than an outright sale under "Project Texas" [Source: ev-1]. This arrangement placed US user data in Oracle's cloud under US control, granted Oracle about a 12.5% stake alongside SoftBank and other investors, while allowing ByteDance to retain a majority interest; Vice President JD Vance led the White House negotiations for this structure, with final ownership completed through 2025 [Source: ev-1].
